subject: RE: Rate limits & Overage terms — pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: rate limits, burst usage & pricing next steps

Hi Sam + Priya —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — great context on Acme's planned feature launches and traffic patterns. Quick recap + a few asks so we can put together a tailored pricing + rate-limit proposal: 

Recap from our call:
- Production footprint today: ~50M tokens/month across search and chat features (mostly search).
- Launch spikes: marketing launches cause short bursts up to ~7M tokens/day for 2–3 days.
- Expected growth: roadmap items point to ~200M tokens/month in 6–12 months if experiments go well.
- Primary constraint: predictable per-request latency for chat; need graceful handling when bursts exceed quota.

Information we need from you to finalize a proposal:
1) Target unit economics: what is your budget target per 1M tokens (ballpark)?
2) Burst behavior: how often do you expect >2M tokens/day bursts and how long do they last?
3) Procurement timeline: any PO/SOW/start date constraints?

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_Q2_2027.pdf and a one-page mutual action plan (Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx) — fills in the milestones we discussed (security review, pilot period, contract).

Next steps I propose:
- You send target $/1M tokens and a short monthly token forecast (current month + next 3 months).
- I'll run unit-economics scenarios (base quota + burst overage) and propose: baseline quota tiers, burst allowance, and overage rates.
- Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with Carlos from our infra team to validate rate-limit behavior and integration approach.

Happy to jump on another call this week if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_Q2_2027.pdf (pricing summary), Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (MAP)
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: rate limits, burst usage & pricing next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Answers below: 

1) Budget target / unit economics:
- Our procurement guidance is $8k–$12k/month initially for inference costs.
- If we normalize, target price is roughly $12 per 1M tokens (we can stretch to $15/1M for guaranteed latency SLAs).

2) Burst behavior:
- Weekly spikes during promos: typical spike ~1.5–2M tokens/day over baseline.
- Product launches: larger spikes up to ~7M tokens/day that last 24–72 hours (2–3 times/year).
- Spikes are front-loaded (first 48 hours) and then drop back to baseline.

3) Procurement timeline:
- We need vendor qualification + security questionnaire answered in 2–3 weeks. Procurement sign-off target end of Q2 (June).

One more ask: how do you handle short-term bursts vs committed quota? We prefer automatic burst protection (so product doesn't see errors) and predictable overage billing rather than sudden throttles.

Appreciate the MAP and pricing sheet — I'll loop in procurement once we have the proposal.

Best,
Sam Chen
Senior PM, Search & AI | Acme Corp
sam.chen@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: rate limits, burst usage & pricing next steps

Sam — perfect, thanks for the details. Based on your numbers I ran a few realistic scenarios and here's what I recommend for an initial commercial structure you can take to procurement: 

Proposal (summary):
- Baseline commitment: 50M tokens/month (matches current).
- Unit price on baseline: $12 / 1M tokens.
- Burst allowance: automatic short-term bursts up to 3x baseline quota within a billing month, intended to cover weekly promos.
- Launch-cap bursts: for launches (multi-day 24–72h spikes) we recommend a pre-authorized burst bucket that lets you scale up to the requested 7M tokens/day. Pre-authorization avoids throttles during launches.
- Overage pricing: for tokens beyond baseline + burst allowance, overage billed at $15 / 1M tokens. Overage invoices are monthly; we can include a cap/credit negotiation in the contract.
- Quota increase SLA: standard request turnaround 48 hours; expedited (same-day) available for pre-approved launch windows with a short form.

Operational guarantees & behavior:
- If bursts exceed allowed limits and no pre-authorized bucket exists, we will gracefully degrade throughput with 429s for non-critical endpoints and prioritized routing for chat endpoints to preserve latency.
- We provide tooling in the Console to simulate quotas and to set up automatic fallback routes to lower-cost model variants during extreme overload.

Next steps I suggest:
1) If this commercial structure looks reasonable, I'll draft a short commercial summary and include it in the MAP.
2) Schedule the security questionnaire kickoff (we can fill SAQ and provide SOC2 artifacts within the 2–3 week window).
3) Technical kickoff with Carlos — propose Mon 29 Mar or Tue 30 Mar, 30 minutes. Which works?

I'll also attach a one-page example of burst/overage math so procurement can see the estimated invoice for a few scenarios.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_Burst_Overage_Example.pdf (one-page cost examples)
From: Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sam Chen <sam.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: rate limits, burst usage & pricing next steps

Thanks Marissa — that structure makes sense and aligns with our procurement constraints. Two quick clarifying questions before we kick to procurement: 

1) Contract language on throttles/credits: If bursts cause degraded availability or increased 429s during a launch window, do you offer any service credit or invoice protection?
2) If we pre-authorize a launch burst and then don't use the full pre-authorized bucket, is there any partial refund or credit in the next invoice?

Procurement asked for a draft commercial summary they can attach to the SOW. If you can get that over today/tomorrow I can loop them in and start the vendor checklist.

Also, Mon 29 Mar 10:00AM PT works for the technical kickoff with Carlos. Please send invite.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Product Operations | Acme Corp
priya@acme.com
